MINUTES

  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  APRIL 25, 2017

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
5:05 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR
PRO TEM HUFF.

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Zerunyan

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

4.  STUDY SESSION ON MUNICIPAL FINANCES

  City Manager Prichard provided a brief overview of the topics to be covered by the
  speakers.

  Doug Jensen, MuniServices, provided an extensive review of the sales tax
  performance for the last quarter. He noted that while retail has decreased across
  the board, new stores coming into the City should boost the sales tax revenue. He
  noted the national and state-wide trend toward on-line purchasing and the effect
  it will have on local sales tax generated by brick and mortar retail stores.

  Discussion ensued regarding collection, pooling and distribution of property tax.

  Discussion then ensued regarding the various business license categories and the
  need to simplify the classifications. Mr. Jensen noted that some solutions might
  include business licenses based on gross receipts and/or flat amounts may be
  simpler to administer.

  City Manager Prichard noted that the City Attorney is working on a “clean up”
  ordinance to simplify some of the categories and procedures.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that since retail is declining and restaurants
  are improving, the COUNCIL should encourage bringing this type of business into
  the City. She then noted that a small hotel is presently in discussions with staff.
  Mr. Jensen commented that hotels are large revenue generators.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ suggested reviewing the transient occupancy tax
  (TOT).

  Jim Godsey, Partner, MGO, provided an extensive presentation of the
  Comprehensive Annual Finance Report (CAFR) and provided detailed information
  regarding the City’s financial position, total assets, total liabilities, net operation
  and net pension liabilities.

  Discussion ensued regarding pension obligations with Mr. Godsey noting that all
  governments must now record their pension liabilities.

  City Manager Prichard referred to the net pension liability of $4 million dollars
  noting that this amount would be reduced by the recent payment of the City’s Pre-
  2013 Small Cities Pool Unfunded Accrued Liability (UAL). He also noted that the
  bond used to pay off the Side Fund will be paid off in 2021.

ADJOURNED
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
APRIL 25, 2017
   City Manager Prichard noted that the category of “revenue from other agencies”
  reflects the receipt of grant funds. Mr. Godsey commented that this indicates staff
  is actively pursuing and competing effectively for outside funding for various
  projects.

  Mr. Godsey explained the roles of governing body and management in financial
  management of the City.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired if the Equestrian Center should be audited
  as a matter of course. Mr. Godsey noted that if the financial statements are
  amiss, it would be a concern and suggested reviewing the revenues and
  expectations as part of the risk analysis if desired. City Manager Prichard
  responded that there are agreed upon procedures between the operator and the
  City’s auditor to give the City a level of confidence when revenues are reported and
  received.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead noted that he reviews the Equestrian
  Center statements every year and has a good handle on the sources of revenue.

  Mr. Godsey explained how the Audit Committee, Staff and COUNCIL work
  together in this process.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commended Mr. Godsey on his presentation and
  experience.

  City Manager Prichard noted that COUNCIL MEMBERS SCHMITZ and
  ZUCKERMAN review all the financial reports in detail and the COUNCIL is well
  served by their participation on the Audit Committee.

  Mr. Godsey referred to the Operations and Internal Control Manual which is in
  the process of being updated and nearing completion. He noted that the Finance
  Department is a good team and has no concerns about how the City is operating
  although he made the following suggestions: 1) Raising the capital threshold to
  $10,000; 2) Switching to a half year depreciation accounting process when
  capital assets are acquired; and 3) Periodically updating the fixed asset lists.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN inquired about the upcoming changes to GASB.
  Terry Robertson, MGO, noted that nothing major will be happening in the next
  two years.

5.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 6:52 p.m., MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF formally adjourned the City Council
  meeting to the regular meeting of April 25, 2017

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk
